source.title: Large Scale Transfer Learning for Differentially Private Image Classification
source.authors: Harsh Mehta; Abhradeep Thakurta; Alexey Kurakin; Ashok Cutkosky

page_placements.theme: Privacy constraints change utility and scaling tradeoffs

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer, batch-size, and model-scaling effects on private transfer learning for ImageNet, a new setting relative to the claim versions. Its measured results are private versus non-private accuracy, not the train–test generalization gap on natural labels.
record.gate_note: Own results test whether optimizer, batch size, and model size change ImageNet test accuracy in DP and non-private transfer learning. The study does not report training error, random-label fitting, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected comparisons, dropout effects, generalization measures, or removal of memorized examples. Values mentioned only as comparison results from cited work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4 through adaptive-versus-momentum optimizer comparisons and V5 through batch-size sweeps at a fixed 10-epoch budget. ImageNet held-out accuracy measures both versions' outcomes; training accuracy or a train–test gap is not required. Private transfer learning supplies a new setting, alongside non-private controls. Full-model LAMB comparisons include an additional layer learning-rate multiplier, so they do not isolate the strict limited-tuning condition of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that scaling public pretraining and model size improves private transfer-learning accuracy and narrows the private-versus-non-private accuracy difference; LAMB improves extreme-batch optimization; and near-zero last-layer initialization enables strong results with a single full-batch update, substantially reducing private-training cost.
record.recipe_differences: Studies private transfer learning on ImageNet using DP-SGD, comparing batch sizes, optimizers, model sizes, and pretraining datasets; it does not use the claim versions' natural-label generalization-gap tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Private test accuracy varies with optimizer, batch size, model and pretraining-data size, last-layer initialization, input resolution, and epoch count.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger pretrained models and more pretraining data improve private ImageNet accuracy and reduce its difference from non-private accuracy. Corrected ViT-H/14-4B full-model values are 81.0% private and 82.5% non-private.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling models and public pretraining data improves private transfer learning; this does not establish width-dependent generalization beyond interpolation.

fits_no_version.finding: Epoch count, input resolution and privacy budget affect last-layer private transfer-learning accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Private last-layer transfer learning can attain high accuracy with one full-batch update and an appropriately chosen input resolution.

record.problems: The work simulates privacy by treating public ImageNet data as sensitive; JFT pretraining datasets are not publicly available. Optimizer and hyperparameter comparisons tune only learning rates, and the paper says the limited exploration was chosen to limit compute. Most results are reported as test accuracy only, without training error or a natural-label train–test gap. Table 4 reports a test accuracy at random chance without giving an exact numerical chance value.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. The study reports additional comparisons and variants, but the extracted table rows emphasize optimizer, batch-size, scaling, and stated hyperparameter results; individual last-layer rows and some duplicated settings were not included.

untested.parts: No fixed-random-label fitting or comparison with natural-label learning.
No width sweep locating zero training error or testing widths beyond that threshold.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.

Training performance is unreported, so equal or better training performance cannot be assessed. No language benchmarks, Adam-to-SGD switching, or isolated weight-decay intervention. Full-model LAMB also tunes a pretrained-layer learning-rate multiplier, exceeding the strictly stated learning-rate/schedule-only comparison.

No language models or controlled demonstration that longer training removes a batch penalty. Learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization and regularization remedies are not individually isolated. Most batch comparisons cover only the extreme 2^17–2^20 range.
Dropout is held at zero; no dropout intervention.
No measured sharpness–generalization-gap relationship or comparison of generalization measures.
No identification and removal of memorized training examples.

missing.what: Non-private single-step full-batch last-layer optimizer comparison: the caption explicitly states that LAMB outperforms momentum SGD and equals Adam for the zero-initialized first update. Numerical curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.
Private ViT-B/16 full-model momentum results at smaller batches: 45.23% at 2^15 and 58.6% at 2^16. Together with 66.5% at 2^17, these locate the best tested batch before the subsequent decline.
missing.locator: Appendix E.4, Table 9; Tables 1 and 6 for comparison and training budget

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly makes training-error reporting a prerequisite for V4 and V5. Both versions directly concern held-out performance. Private-versus-non-private accuracy differences are distinct from train–test generalization gaps. Fixed 10-epoch budgets are specified in Tables 6–7. At fixed privacy budget, noise changes with batch size, so private batch results concern the combined privacy-adjusted recipe. Table 7 also contradicts the blanket claim that only learning rate was tuned by listing a pretrained-layer multiplier. Several rows bear on two versions with opposite directions; their problem fields state the version-specific states. Last-layer table rows explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training, memorization-capacity test, or natural-label training-versus-test error comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Optimizer comparisons concern private transfer-learning accuracy and do not measure natural-label generalization relative to training performance under the stated limited-tuning comparison.
Batch-size comparisons are reported, but they concern private transfer-learning accuracy and do not establish a generalization gap under fixed epoch budgets as specified.
No dropout intervention or test-error comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining comparison.
